- Added ROE data fetch script to enhance financial data coverage.

- Adjusted documentation for clarity and up-to-date usage instructions.
- Removed deprecated scripts and data files for a cleaner project structure.

llm.summary: The skill is mostly coherent for a local stock-analysis web app, but there are mismatches between what the registry declared and what the code/instructions actually require (notably AI provider credentials and system-level installs), and the included install scripts perform global installs — review before running.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (stock quotes, limit-up tracking, shareholder dynamics, UI) aligns with the included backend, frontend, and data files. However the repository/code expects and documents AI provider configuration (AI_PROVIDER, AI_API_KEY) and third-party connectors (pywencai, akshare), yet the registry metadata lists no required environment variables or credentials — a mismatch between declared requirements and actual code.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and the code keep scope to stock data, analysis, and an AI chat assistant. Runtime steps reference local JSON/DB files and standard network APIs (qt.gtimg.cn, pywencai, akshare, and external AI providers). Nothing in SKILL.md or code instructs the agent to read unrelated system files or to exfiltrate data to unexpected endpoints. The AI chat component will send user messages (and the system prompt) to whichever AI provider you configure.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no formal install spec in the registry (instruction-only), but the bundle includes scripts/install.sh and start.sh which the docs recommend running. SKILL.md and README instruct installing Node.js and running npm -g jsdom (global npm install). Global npm installs and modifying NODE_PATH are system-level changes worth cautioning about; the install scripts could run arbitrary shell commands — review scripts/install.sh before executing or run in an isolated environment.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The registry declares no required env vars, yet code and documentation expect AI_PROVIDER and AI_API_KEY (and optionally AI_BASE_URL, AI_MODEL). AI_API_KEY would be sent to external AI provider endpoints when AI is enabled. The default provider in code is 'silence' which avoids sending data, but SKILL.md and backend/AI_CONFIG.md explicitly instruct users to set API keys and .env files. This mismatch (no declared credentials vs. code that uses them) is a proportionality/visibility concern — supplying an API key grants the skill network access to that provider using your key.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not marked always:true and does not request special platform privileges. It reads and writes local files (portfolio_data.json, memos.json, stock_codes.json, a local sqlite DB) which is expected for a portfolio app. The install scripts may set environment variables (NODE_PATH) and perform global npm installs, which affect the host system but do not alter other skills' configs.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
What to check before installing/using:
- Do not run scripts/install.sh or start.sh without reading them first. They perform system-level installs (npm -g jsdom) and set NODE_PATH. Run them in a VM/container if you want to be safe.
- The code will send chat messages to whichever AI provider you configure. If you set AI_API_KEY, that key will be used by the backend to call external AI endpoints — only provide keys you trust and prefer using providers you control.
- The registry metadata lists no required env vars, but the repository expects AI_PROVIDER/AI_API_KEY (optional if using rule-based 'silence'). This mismatch is intentional design but you should be aware: by default AI is disabled, but enabling it will transmit messages and prompts to third-party services.
- The app reads/writes local files (portfolio_data.json, memos.json, sqlite DB). These are local user data — back them up if you care about them or inspect the files first.
- Network activity (qt.gtimg.cn, pywencai, akshare, and AI provider URLs) is necessary for functionality; expect external requests. If you need stricter privacy, run the skill offline or block network access.
- If unsure, run the skill in an isolated environment and inspect install/start scripts and any network calls (or run with AI_PROVIDER=silence to avoid sending chat data to external services).
